reasoning_steps: Data from major scientific agencies including NASA, NOAA, and the European Environment Agency consistently demonstrate a statistically significant, long-term decline in Arctic sea ice extent since satellite monitoring began in the late 1970s. Both summer minimums and winter maximums show downward trends that go beyond short-term interannual variability.

Official government reports from the U.S. House Committee on the Budget and reports from major news organizations confirm that the United States' gross national debt officially surpassed the $34 trillion mark on December 29, 2023. By early 2024, the figure had climbed even higher, exceeding $34.4 trillion by February 2024.

The claim that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines alter or permanently change human DNA is scientifically false. Authoritative medical and research institutions, including the NIH's National Human Genome Research Institute, Weill Cornell Medicine, and Nebraska Medicine, have clarified that mRNA cannot alter DNA. The mRNA from the vaccines operates strictly in the cytoplasm, is unable to enter the cell nucleus where DNA is housed, lacks the necessary enzymes (such as reverse transcriptase) to integrate into the host genome, and is naturally degraded by the cell shortly after delivering its instructions.

Multiple sources and studies verify that AI models can pass the US bar exam. While the original study's claim that GPT-4 scored in the 90th percentile (top 10%) was disputed by subsequent MIT research—which argued it actually scored around the 68th percentile—both studies confirm that the model successfully passed the exam. A score in the 68th percentile is still above the average human test-taker (the 50th percentile). Furthermore, newer AI models have continued to show improvement, with many consistently scoring above human averages.

Historical data confirms that Congress has not passed all of its individual, regular appropriations bills before the start of the fiscal year (October 1) since Fiscal Year 1997 (which was enacted in 1996). Since then, the government has been funded through temporary continuing resolutions, omnibus spending packages, or legislative packages passed after the start of the fiscal year, rather than the timely passage of all 12 discrete appropriations bills.
